case_name: Bhawna Garg and another v University Of Delhi & Ors
facts: The Delhi University issued a Bulletin of Information for admissions to the Under-Graduate Degree Courses for the academic session 2011-2012 (for short 'the Bulletin').
Para 2 of the Bulletin dealt with admissions to MBBS course.
Only female candidates were to be admitted in LHMC.

Candidates for 15% seats were to be selected directly by the Directorate General of Health Sciences (DGHS) based on the result of the examination conducted by the CBSE, New Delhi, as per the directions of this Court.

The Bulletin further provides that besides the 15% seats directly filled up by the DGHS based on the examination conducted by the CBSE, New Delhi, and the NGOI, all other candidates have to appear in the DUMET and will be admitted to the MBBS course on the basis of their merit in the category in which they have applied.
The appellants applied as female general category candidates and also took and cleared the DUMET.

However, on account of their lower rank in the merit list of candidates who cleared the DUMET, the appellants could not be admitted to any of the seats in the three government medical colleges under the university.
issues: Is the reservation of as many as 30 seats in the MBBS course in LHMC violative of Art. 14 of the Constitution?

Is the procedure adopted by the Government of India in nominating the candidates for the 30 seats without holding a common entrance test for determination of their merit contrary to the Medical Council of India Regulations on Graduate Medical Education, 1997?
petitioner_arguments: The Constitution Bench judgment of this Court in Kumari Chitra Ghosh & Anr. v. Union of India & Ors. [1969 (2) SCC 228] has lost its relevance inasmuch as the entire procedure for medical admissions has undergone a sea-change during the past four decades after the aforesaid judgment was rendered in 1969.

The MCI Regulations and in particular Regulation 5 thereof mandates that the selection of students to medical colleges shall be based solely on merit of the candidate and for determination of merit the criteria laid down in Regulation 5 of the MCI Regulations has to be adopted uniformly throughout the country.

There are no exceptions provided in Regulation 5 to holding of a competitive entrance examination and even candidates belonging to the reserved categories including the physically handicapped with 70% disability are required to appear in the competitive entrance examination to secure admission to the medical courses.
court_reasoning: The High Court held that in Kumari Chitra Ghosh & Anr. v. Union of India & Ors. [1969 (2) SCC 228] a Constitution Bench of this Court has considered the challenge to reservation of seats for certain categories of students on the ground that it is violative of Art. 14 of the Constitution and has held the reservation to be constitutionally valid.

The High Court further held that even though a sea-change may have taken place since the judgment was delivered by this Court in Kumari Chitra Ghosh 1969 Indlaw SC 525 (supra), it is only for this Court to hold that the ratio of Kumari Chitra Ghosh 1969 Indlaw SC 525 (supra) has become irrelevant.
holding: The High Court held that the reservation of as many as 30 seats in the MBBS course in LHMC was constitutionally valid.
The appellants' writ petitions were dismissed.
